faq.q: Is AI a mandatory school subject in Canada?
faq.a: No. There is no Canada-wide mandatory AI class; education is provincial. B.C. embeds AI literacy inside Applied Design, Skills & Technologies (ADST) and Career Education, and New Brunswick is weaving AI literacy across K–12 from September 2026.

faq.q: Can my child use ChatGPT for homework?
faq.a: It depends on the assignment and the school's approved tools. Many AI tools require users to be 13+. Ask the teacher which level (green/yellow/red) applies and which tools are approved.

faq.q: What happens if AI-generated work is submitted as their own?
faq.a: Schools treat it as plagiarism under academic-integrity policies. Encourage your child to disclose AI use honestly using the templates in this platform.

Schools vet tools for privacy compliance; for example, the Vancouver School Board approved Microsoft Copilot with Enterprise Data Protection. Remind children never to enter personal details into any AI chat.

faq.q: How can I help at home?
faq.a: Use the 'attempt → compare → revise' pattern together, listen to lessons in your home language, and talk about what AI got wrong.

about.title: About SI Academy
about.body: SI Academy (Super Intelligence Academy) is an open-source learning platform built to support Canada's National AI Literacy Initiative (launched 9 September 2026 with Amii) and provincial curricula. It is not affiliated with the Government of Canada or Amii. Content is summarised from public briefings and should be verified against your district's policies.
